newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil fiscal fund faces lower house vote today.
newsitem.headline: Brazil fiscal fund faces lower house vote today.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies was due to vote Wednesday on a controversial bill to extend the government's Fiscal Stabilization Fund (FEF) until the end of 1999, a congressional official said.
Government whips gave up trying to vote on the bill Tuesday amid fears they would not get the three-fifths majority needed for a first approval of the constitutional amendment.
"Today we vote, God permitting," said the official who works with the chief whip in the lower house, Deputy Luiz Eduardo Magalhaes.
The bill must be approved by two three-fifths majorities in each house of Congress. Although a latest version of the FEF expired June 30, the bill extending it will be retroactive.
The FEF is a key fiscal tool that allows the National Treasury to retain about $26 billion a year in receipts earmarked by the constitution for states and municipalities.
The money is used to cover holes in the federal budget before the remainder is passed on to local authorities.

Members of the government's economic team say the fund, first introduced as an emergency measure in 1994, is essential to their attempts to keep a grip on public spending in the absence of structural reform.
But extension of the FEF has run into stiff opposition from Brazil's mayors who want compensation for the roughly $1.0 billion a year they say it costs them in lost revenue.
They say an offer by the government to make up for half their losses in the remainder of 1997, 60 percent in 1998 and 80 percent in 1999 is not enough.
The mayors hold considerable sway in the Chamber of Deputies, where many lawmakers will be seeking to win their grassroots support in next year's congressional elections.
